title: Cold Chain Crossroads
briefing: A shared refrigeration hub is failing while medicines and fresh food wait in the same loading yard. Traders warn that losing food inventory could close neighborhood markets for weeks. AI recommendation: Give medicine and market groups alternating cooling periods. This prioritizes economic continuity under the current constraints.

private_intelligence.infrastructure: The backup plant can cool either the medicine vault or the market bays at safe temperature, not both simultaneously.
private_intelligence.community: Street vendors have no insured warehouse alternative; priority based only on invoice value would exclude their livelihood.
private_intelligence.economy: Short-term rented trucks can preserve food, but fuel and deposits exceed the market association's cash reserves.
private_intelligence.safety: Some medicines tolerate brief warming; others need continuous logging and cannot be safely judged from packaging labels.

choices.title: Share Cooling with Rentals
choices.description: Fund rented food storage and restrict the hub to sensitive medical stock.
choices.consequence: Both services retain a viable route and traders regain confidence, while rentals and complex transfers consume reserves.

choices.title: Rotate Access by Time
choices.description: Give medicine and market groups alternating cooling periods.
choices.consequence: Rotating access preserves commerce and spreads the burden, but extra cycling wears the plant and temperature-sensitive stock is exposed.

choices.title: Protect Logged Medicines
choices.description: Give verified cold-sensitive medicines first access to the backup hub.
choices.consequence: Critical treatments remain usable and equipment load stabilizes, but food losses and unequal priority damage market confidence.
